the step-like regions on AC magnetic field dependences of Tmg(ho), revealed in the measurements of AC magnetic susceptibility, can be interpreted as the result of the existence of structural inhomogeneities within the superconducting grains.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of structural inhomogeneities of superconducting ceramics on intragranual properties of YBaCuO and BiPbSbSrCaCuO superconducting systems.
the influence of structural inhomogeneities (grain boundaries, precipitations, etc.) on the intragranular properties of high-Tc superconducting ceramics.
the study of the effect of structural inhomogeneities of Y-based and Bi-based ceramics on intragranual superconducting properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the observed steps in Tmg(ho), which were found for all samples, are caused by the existence of different superconducting regions in granuls, and that the steps at the temperature scale depend on composition and type of the atoms substituting the copper in the samples.
the step-like regions are related to the existence of structural inhomogeneities in the superconducting granules.
the step-like regions in Tmg(ho)-curves are related to the inhomogeneity of the superconducting phase in granules.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the steps on Tmg(ho)-curves can be considered as a manifestation of a new type of inhomogeneites.
the steps are related with inhomogeneities of the granular structure of superconductors.
the step-like regions on Tmg(ho ) curves are due to the presence of structural inhomogeneties in the form of superconducting grains with different critical temperatures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of structural inhomogeneities in superconductors is not a unique phenomenon and that the influence of inclusions on intragranual superconducting properties is not always the same.

the step-like regions on Tmg(ho), which are related with the inhomogeneities in superconducting properties, are not only a characteristic feature for Bi-based superconducting ceramics but also for Y-based ones.

the step-like regions in AC magnetic field dependence of hystereses losses peak temperatures for superconducting grains can be considered as an evidence for existence of structural inhomogeneities inside the superconducting grains.
